transcript.text: Hi everyone, I'd like to get us started on discussing Mr. Lewis's potential enrollment in our remote-monitoring program after his heart-failure discharge. As we know, our standard workflow is to review the clinical, technology, and home-support requirements together before I finalize any enrollment and configuration decisions. I'd like to hear from cardiology nursing, clinical informatics, and social work so we can put together a complete picture. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: I can start with the clinical picture. Mr. Lewis's most recent echocardiogram shows a left-ventricular ejection fraction of exactly 32%. Our program's clinical eligibility criterion is an ejection fraction of 35% or lower, so he meets the criterion. I have this result from the specialist's signed report.

transcript.text: On the technology side, I should share an important finding: Mr. Lewis's apartment has no reliable internet service. However, our informatics team has a cellular monitoring hub reserved for him. The critical detail is that this hub must be configured during device setup for the connected scale and blood-pressure monitor to transmit readings — without that configuration step, the devices won't be able to send data back to us.
